note: agent-lifted from VA's manuals (pilot steps 2 and 3)

concepts.label: Transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: A hardware failure of a transmitting optical laser that extinguishes the affected channel and causes loss of signal at the far-end receiver.
concepts.example: The laser in a VA-TPD-400 stops emitting, so its channel is dark and the remote terminal reports OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: Card failure
concepts.gloss: A card-level hardware failure that removes local traffic and monitoring functions and can cause remote loss of signal while masking subordinate traffic alarms.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-400 card loses power, its received traffic disappears, telemetry becomes silent, and the far end sees loss of signal.

concepts.label: Receiver degradation
concepts.gloss: Deterioration confined to an optical receiver that introduces receive errors without impairing the optical path or other channels.
concepts.example: One VA-OTN-LC-200 receiver develops excess noise and reports pre-FEC errors while adjacent channels remain normal.

concepts.label: Laser ageing
concepts.gloss: Progressive wear of a transmit laser that requires rising bias current and precedes eventual laser failure.
concepts.example: A transponder's LBC rises from 100% to 123% of beginning-of-life current and triggers LASER_BIAS_HIGH before the laser fails.

concepts.label: Margin erosion
concepts.gloss: A gradual reduction in an optical channel's performance margin, typically due to cumulative component ageing along its path.
concepts.example: A channel's margin declines slowly over several months even though it remains in service.

concepts.label: Fibre break
concepts.gloss: A physical cut or break in an optical fibre that interrupts light propagation on the affected span.
concepts.example: Excavation cuts the incoming fibre, causing AMP_INPUT_LOS at the next amplifier and OCH_LOS on carried channels.

concepts.label: EDFA dead
concepts.gloss: Complete failure of an erbium-doped fibre amplifier, resulting in no amplified output and loss of every channel traversing it.
concepts.example: The preceding VA-OA-ILA loses its pump and emits no output light, so all downstream wavelengths are lost.

concepts.label: jumper pulled
concepts.gloss: Disconnection of an optical patch jumper, especially at an OMS input, that removes light from the connected path.
concepts.example: A technician removes the pre-amplifier's OMS input jumper and the card raises OMS_LOS_P.

concepts.label: WSS ingress port failure
concepts.gloss: Failure or blocking of one wavelength-selective-switch ingress port that blocks all channels arriving on its ROADM degree while leaving other degrees unaffected.
concepts.example: The west-degree WSS input port fails, blocking every west-arriving wavelength at the node while east-degree traffic continues.

concepts.label: high span loss
concepts.gloss: Excessive attenuation across a fibre span that lowers received optical level and can lead to degraded framing or complete loss of input light.
concepts.example: A damaged splice adds 12 dB of span loss, causing OTU_SD and eventually AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: Noise figure degradation
concepts.gloss: Degradation of an EDFA's noise figure that reduces channel OSNR despite normal amplifier output power.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-PRE maintains its target output power, but all channels lose 3 dB of OSNR and an OTU_SD alarm appears.

concepts.label: DGD increase
concepts.gloss: An increase in differential group delay on an optical path that impairs coherent signal recovery and may cause degradation or frame loss.
concepts.example: DGD rises during a fibre disturbance until the receiver crosses its degrade threshold and raises OTU_SD.

concepts.label: WSS passband offset
concepts.gloss: A WSS filter alignment fault that shifts or narrows one channel's passband, degrading signal quality while measured output power may remain normal.
concepts.example: A ROADM passband shifts 4 GHz from the carrier, leaving channel power normal but causing poor OSNR and OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: fast SOP event
concepts.gloss: A rapid state-of-polarization change faster than the coherent receiver can track, causing transient signal degradation or loss of frame.
concepts.example: A fibre disturbance causes an SOP-RATE spike beyond tracking speed and the receiver briefly raises OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: contaminated connector
concepts.gloss: Optical connector contamination that introduces loss or reflections sufficient to degrade an affected channel.
concepts.example: Dust on a line connector raises pre-FEC BER above the degrade threshold and produces OTU_SD.

concepts.label: Any failure
concepts.gloss: A wildcard cause representing any underlying fault capable of producing the associated generic defect, protection, or backward-indication alarm.
concepts.example: PROT_ACTIVE is attributed to any failure on the working path when no more specific root cause has yet been identified.

concepts.label: Gain loss
concepts.gloss: Partial loss of EDFA amplification that lowers composite output and degrades OSNR across all amplified channels.
concepts.example: An amplifier delivers 3 dB less gain than its target, causing AMP_GAIN_OOR and low output on every wavelength.

concepts.label: Pump ageing
concepts.gloss: Progressive deterioration of an EDFA pump laser that requires increasing drive current to maintain gain and ultimately triggers an end-of-life alarm.
concepts.example: PUMP-I climbs to 121% of beginning-of-life current on a VA-OA-BST and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: Gain tilt
concepts.gloss: A wavelength-dependent amplifier gain imbalance that makes channels near one spectral band edge lower in power than others.
concepts.example: The long-wavelength edge channels leave an EDFA 2 dB below central channels while total output remains acceptable.

concepts.label: Fabric failure
concepts.gloss: Failure of an OTN switch fabric that interrupts all ODUs crossing the switch and propagates ODU-AIS on each cross-connected ODU.
concepts.example: A VA-OTNSW fabric fault drops every traversing ODU, raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL, and forwards ODU-AIS downstream.

concepts.label: Misconnection
concepts.gloss: An erroneous OTN cross-connect that routes one ODU to the wrong destination without necessarily producing an optical-layer symptom.
concepts.example: ODU 7 is provisioned to the wrong client port, producing ODU_TIM although optical power remains normal.

concepts.label: Port failure
concepts.gloss: Failure of a client interface port or its optic that takes the associated client service out of operation.
concepts.example: The optic in a VA-CP-100GE fails, raising EQPT_PORT_FAIL and dropping the 100GE service.

concepts.label: WSS attenuation drift
concepts.gloss: A gradual increase in a WSS channel attenuation setting that lowers the power of one routed wavelength after the ROADM node.
concepts.example: One channel's WSS attenuation creeps upward by 2 dB, and OCM measurements show that wavelength low after the node.

concepts.label: No light
concepts.gloss: A receiver condition in which no optical energy is detected on the expected channel.
concepts.example: The far-end receiver measures power below its detection threshold and raises OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: dLOS
concepts.gloss: A digital loss-of-signal defect indicating that the receiver cannot detect a valid digital signal.
concepts.example: After input power collapses, the line receiver asserts dLOS even though the card remains powered.

concepts.label: Loss of OTU frame
concepts.gloss: A defect in which the receiver can no longer acquire or maintain valid Optical Transport Unit framing.
concepts.example: Severe optical impairment prevents OTU frame alignment and causes OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: Card failure
concepts.gloss: The observed state that an equipment card is nonfunctional because of a card-level fault.
concepts.example: A line card fails self-test and is reported in the card-failure state.

concepts.label: dEQ
concepts.gloss: A digital equipment-quality defect indicating that the received signal quality is below the equipment's acceptable threshold.
concepts.example: Excessive decoder errors cause the receiver to assert dEQ before complete frame loss.

concepts.label: traffic alarms masked
synonyms: traffic alarms masked by the equipment alarm
concepts.gloss: A state in which a dominant equipment alarm suppresses or obscures lower-level traffic alarms.
concepts.example: EQPT_CARD_FAIL is active, so individual OTU and ODU traffic alarms from that card are masked.

concepts.label: Degraded light: low power, low OSNR, high DGD, passband penalty, receiver penalty, slow margin decline
concepts.gloss: A broad optical degradation state encompassing low power, poor OSNR, excessive DGD, filtering or receiver penalties, or slowly declining margin.
concepts.example: A channel still carries traffic but has low power and OSNR together with rising pre-FEC BER.

concepts.label: Pre-FEC errors once the degradation is larger than the channel margin
concepts.gloss: Pre-FEC decoding errors that appear once optical degradation exceeds the channel's available margin.
concepts.example: When margin falls below zero, PREFEC-BER rises from negligible values to 1×10^-4.

concepts.label: loss of frame if much larger
concepts.gloss: Loss of frame occurring when an already significant signal degradation becomes substantially larger.
concepts.example: A channel first raises OTU_SD and then loses OTU framing after another 5 dB of loss is introduced.

concepts.label: Fast SOP change beyond tracking speed
concepts.gloss: A state-of-polarization variation whose rate exceeds the coherent receiver's polarization-tracking capability.
concepts.example: SOP-RATE spikes during fibre movement and the receiver briefly loses frame.

concepts.label: Errored seconds
concepts.gloss: One-second measurement intervals containing at least one counted transmission error.
concepts.example: ES-15 reports 18 errored seconds during the current 15-minute interval.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS is sent downstream
concepts.gloss: The consequent condition in which ODU alarm-indication signal is transmitted downstream after an upstream OTU defect.
concepts.example: On OTU frame loss, the line card inserts ODU-AIS into every contained ODU toward downstream clients.

concepts.label: OTU-BDI is returned
concepts.gloss: The consequent condition in which OTU backward defect indication is sent toward the far-end transmitter.
concepts.example: A receiver losing OTU frame returns OTU-BDI to the transmitting terminal.

concepts.label: Laser off or failed
concepts.gloss: A channel condition in which its transmitting laser is intentionally off or has failed and therefore emits no usable carrier.
concepts.example: The line laser on channel 43 fails and the channel disappears from the optical spectrum.

concepts.label: loss of signal
concepts.gloss: A far-end receiver indication that the expected transmitted optical signal is absent.
concepts.example: When the local transmit laser fails, the remote receiver declares loss of signal.

concepts.label: received traffic lost
concepts.gloss: Local loss of all traffic being received through the affected card or interface.
concepts.example: A failed muxponder card stops delivering its locally received client traffic.

concepts.label: monitoring silent
concepts.gloss: Loss of telemetry or supervision output from an affected equipment card.
concepts.example: After a card processor failure, performance counters and status reports stop updating.

concepts.label: Errors
concepts.gloss: Transmission errors confined to the affected receiver rather than shared by the optical path or other channels.
concepts.example: One receiver records high pre-FEC BER while another receiver on the same optical channel remains clean.

concepts.label: normal
concepts.gloss: An unaffected state in which the optical path and channels outside the identified receiver continue to operate within limits.
concepts.example: A degraded receiver reports errors, but the path power and all neighboring wavelengths remain normal.

concepts.label: LBC rising
concepts.gloss: An upward trend in laser bias current as the transmitter compensates for laser ageing.
concepts.example: LBC increases from 102% to 116% over six months while output power is maintained.

concepts.label: precedes transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: An incipient indication expected to occur before complete transmit-laser failure.
concepts.example: Sustained high LBC provides warning weeks before the laser can no longer produce output.

concepts.label: Slow decline of the channel's margin, usually from ageing of components along the path
concepts.gloss: A slow reduction in channel performance margin observed at the receiver, usually reflecting ageing along the end-to-end path.
concepts.example: The receiver's estimated margin falls from 4 dB to 2 dB over a year.

concepts.label: OTU frame lost, light present
concepts.gloss: Loss of OTU frame alignment while optical light is still detected, distinguishing quality impairment from total signal loss.
concepts.example: OPR remains at −10 dBm, but the receiver raises OTU_LOF because it cannot decode the frame.

concepts.label: Errors above the degrade threshold (margin under about 1 dB)
concepts.gloss: An error level above the signal-degrade threshold, typically corresponding to less than about 1 dB of remaining margin.
concepts.example: PREFEC-BER crosses the configured threshold at 0.8 dB margin and raises OTU_SD.

concepts.label: Far end reports a defect on this card's transmitted signal
concepts.gloss: A backward indication that the remote receiver has detected a defect in the signal transmitted by this card.
concepts.example: The remote terminal loses frame and returns OTU-BDI to the local transmitter.

concepts.label: Transmit laser fault detected
concepts.gloss: An equipment-detected fault in the transmit laser or its drive circuitry.
concepts.example: Laser supervision detects no optical output despite drive current and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

concepts.label: Card hardware fault
concepts.gloss: A hardware defect detected within an equipment card rather than on its carried traffic.
concepts.example: A card's internal power rail fails self-test and raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

concepts.label: LBC above 120 % of beginning of life (internal supervision)
concepts.gloss: An internal supervision threshold state where laser bias current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: An LBC reading of 123% activates LASER_BIAS_HIGH.

concepts.label: The EDFA cards run in automatic gain control (AGC).
concepts.gloss: The operating state in which an EDFA automatically adjusts pump drive to maintain a configured gain.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA increases pump current after its input level falls so that its 20 dB gain target is retained.

concepts.label: The gain target is provisioned at turn-up equal to the attenuation of the fibre span ahead of the card.
concepts.gloss: The provisioned EDFA gain value set at turn-up to compensate for the attenuation of the following fibre span.
concepts.example: For an 18 dB outgoing span, the booster is provisioned with an 18 dB gain target.

concepts.label: Under AGC, a drop of input level
concepts.gloss: A reduction in composite optical power entering an EDFA while it is operating under automatic gain control.
concepts.example: IN-PWR falls by 3 dB after an upstream fibre loss.

concepts.label: an equal drop of output level
concepts.gloss: A reduction in EDFA output power equal to an input-power reduction when constant gain is maintained.
concepts.example: With gain fixed at 20 dB, a 3 dB drop at IN-PWR produces a 3 dB drop at OUT-PWR.

concepts.label: the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) of all channels degrades with it
concepts.gloss: A reduction of optical signal-to-noise ratio across all channels associated with a common line or amplifier impairment.
concepts.example: After amplifier input power falls, every wavelength shows a 2 dB OSNR penalty.

concepts.label: A card with no input light
concepts.gloss: A state in which an optical card receives no detectable light at its input.
concepts.example: A pre-amplifier reports IN-PWR below threshold after the incoming fibre is disconnected.

concepts.label: no output light
concepts.gloss: Absence of optical output from an amplifier or card, affecting all channels it should emit.
concepts.example: A dead VA-OA-ILA has valid input light but OUT-PWR shows no output.

concepts.label: Other conditions at the input
concepts.gloss: Input-side optical properties or impairments other than total input-light loss that are presented to a card.
concepts.example: Input channels arrive with unequal powers and an existing OSNR penalty.

concepts.label: are passed through to the output
concepts.gloss: A propagation state in which input conditions remain present at a card's output rather than being removed by the card.
concepts.example: An incoming channel's OSNR penalty remains visible after passing through an amplifier.

concepts.label: Every hut terminates the optical supervisory channel (OSC) and launches its own OSC onto the next span
concepts.gloss: The topology condition that each amplifier hut terminates the incoming OSC and originates a new OSC for the next span.
concepts.example: Hut B receives the OSC from span A–B and launches a separate OSC over span B–C.

concepts.label: an OSC failure is confined to the span on which it occurs
concepts.gloss: A containment condition in which an OSC failure affects only the individual span where it occurs.
concepts.example: Loss of OSC on span B–C does not suppress the separately regenerated OSC on span C–D.

concepts.label: all channels lost
concepts.gloss: Simultaneous absence of every wavelength channel traversing an affected common optical element.
concepts.example: Failure of an in-line EDFA removes all 80 channels from the downstream spectrum.

concepts.label: low output
concepts.gloss: Composite amplifier output power below the expected level across all carried channels.
concepts.example: OUT-PWR is 4 dB below target and each wavelength is correspondingly low.

concepts.label: OSNR down
concepts.gloss: Reduced optical signal-to-noise ratio affecting all channels sharing the impaired amplifier or line section.
concepts.example: OCM reports a 2 dB OSNR reduction on every channel after amplifier gain loss.

concepts.label: output power normal
concepts.gloss: A state in which measured optical output power remains within its expected range despite another signal-quality impairment.
concepts.example: A misaligned WSS filter leaves channel power at −2 dBm even though pre-FEC BER rises.

concepts.label: PUMP-I climbs to maintain gain
concepts.gloss: A rising EDFA pump-current trend on the affected card as control circuitry compensates for pump ageing to preserve gain.
concepts.example: PUMP-I on one pre-amplifier rises from 100% to 118% while its gain remains on target.

concepts.label: ends in the end-of-life alarm
concepts.gloss: The terminal pump-ageing state in which the affected amplifier card declares that its pump has reached its service-life threshold.
concepts.example: At 121% PUMP-I, the card raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: channels low
concepts.gloss: A gain-tilt symptom in which wavelengths at one spectral band edge have lower power than the rest.
concepts.example: The three highest-frequency channels measure 2 dB below mid-band channels.

concepts.label: Loss of light at IN-PWR
concepts.gloss: A loss-of-light state detected by the composite input-power measurement of an amplifier or OMS termination.
concepts.example: IN-PWR drops below the LOS threshold at an OLA and AMP_INPUT_LOS is raised.

concepts.label: OSC not received
concepts.gloss: A state in which the optical supervisory channel receiver cannot detect or decode the OSC on its span.
concepts.example: A fibre cut prevents the next hut from receiving OSC, causing OSC_LOS.

concepts.label: No light at OUT-PWR with input light present
concepts.gloss: An amplifier failure signature in which input light is present but no output light is produced.
concepts.example: IN-PWR reads −8 dBm while OUT-PWR is below detection, causing AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: Gain more than 2 dB from target
concepts.gloss: An amplifier gain measurement differing from its provisioned target by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: Measured gain is 16.5 dB against a 19 dB target, raising AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: PUMP-I above 120 % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: An EDFA pump-current threshold state above 120% of its beginning-of-life drive current.
concepts.example: A PUMP-I value of 122% causes AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: The switch forwards ODU-AIS on each ODU it cross-connects.
concepts.gloss: The OTN-switch behavior of propagating ODU-AIS on every ODU that the fabric cross-connects.
concepts.example: ODU-AIS received on ODU2 is forwarded through VA-OTNSW to ODU2's egress.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS
concepts.gloss: An ODU alarm-indication signal marking downstream payload as unavailable because of an upstream defect.
concepts.example: A client port receives ODU-AIS after the upstream OTU loses frame.

concepts.label: a misdirected ODU
concepts.gloss: An ODU delivered along an unintended cross-connect path or to the wrong destination.
concepts.example: The ODU expected at client port A appears at client port B and triggers a trace mismatch.

concepts.label: the client service down
concepts.gloss: Loss of availability of the client service associated with a failed port, path, or payload.
concepts.example: A failed 100GE client optic makes the connected customer service unavailable.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS or a misdirected ODU
concepts.gloss: A received ODU state indicating either upstream alarm substitution or delivery of the wrong ODU.
concepts.example: A client port sees either an ODU-AIS pattern or an unexpected trail trace after a switch fault.

concepts.label: SNCP is configured
concepts.gloss: A protection state in which a client service has both working and protection ODU paths under SNCP selection.
concepts.example: A 100GE service is duplicated onto two diverse ODU paths terminating at one selector.

concepts.label: the selector has a defect-free path to choose
concepts.gloss: Availability of at least one SNCP branch without defects for the receiving selector to choose.
concepts.example: The working ODU raises AIS, so the selector chooses the clean protection ODU.

concepts.label: the service takes a hit only
concepts.gloss: A brief client-service interruption incurred during protection selection rather than a sustained outage.
concepts.example: The service loses several milliseconds of traffic while SNCP switches to the protection path.

concepts.label: interrupted
concepts.gloss: Simultaneous interruption of all ODUs traversing an OTN switch fabric.
concepts.example: A fabric reset stops every ODU cross-connected through the switch.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS forwarded
concepts.gloss: Propagation of ODU-AIS on each affected ODU through the switch toward downstream termination points.
concepts.example: Following a fabric defect, AIS is sent on every impacted ODU egress.

concepts.label: cross-connected to the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: A one-ODU routing condition in which the cross-connect delivers that ODU to an unintended endpoint.
concepts.example: ODU 12 is connected to client port 6 instead of client port 4.

concepts.label: no optical symptom
concepts.gloss: Absence of an optical-layer power or quality anomaly despite a logical routing defect affecting one ODU.
concepts.example: A misconnected ODU has normal channel power and OSNR but fails its trail-trace check.

concepts.label: failed
concepts.gloss: A nonfunctional state of a client port and its associated optical transceiver.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-400GE optic stops operating and the port is marked failed.

concepts.label: Switching is per channel
concepts.gloss: A ROADM switching model in which each wavelength is independently selected and routed at an egress degree.
concepts.example: At one ROADM, channel 21 is routed east while channel 22 is routed south.

concepts.label: A line-wide impairment on an ingress degree therefore continues as a per-channel impairment on each channel routed onward.
concepts.gloss: A common impairment arriving on an entire ingress line that becomes attached to each individual wavelength as those channels are routed onward.
concepts.example: All west-degree channels acquire an OSNR penalty and retain it after being split across east and south egresses.

concepts.label: An upstream power loss within that range
concepts.gloss: A reduction in channel power originating upstream that lies within the downstream node's leveling range.
concepts.example: A wavelength arrives 2 dB low after a span event but remains within the ROADM equalizer's correction range.

concepts.label: is levelled out at the node
concepts.gloss: Restoration of an incoming channel's power to its configured target by node-level attenuation control.
concepts.example: A channel arriving 2 dB low is equalized back to −2 dBm at the ROADM output.

concepts.label: the OSNR penalty it caused stays
concepts.gloss: Persistence of an upstream-created OSNR impairment even after a node restores the channel's power level.
concepts.example: The ROADM corrects channel power, but the earlier 2 dB OSNR loss remains measurable.

concepts.label: a larger loss
concepts.gloss: An upstream power reduction exceeding the node's available leveling or compensation range.
concepts.example: A 10 dB input loss cannot be corrected by a WSS with only 6 dB of adjustment.

concepts.label: is passed on as low power
concepts.gloss: Propagation of a channel beyond a node at a power below its target because the node cannot fully compensate its loss.
concepts.example: A severely attenuated wavelength leaves the ROADM still 4 dB low.

concepts.label: passes through
concepts.gloss: A condition or impairment that propagates through an intermediate optical element without being terminated.
concepts.example: An existing OSNR penalty remains on a wavelength after it crosses the ROADM.

concepts.label: Attenuation creeps above its setting
concepts.gloss: A slow unintended increase in the WSS attenuation applied to one channel relative to its configured setting.
concepts.example: A WSS setting provisioned at 3 dB drifts to 5 dB over several weeks.

concepts.label: low in power
concepts.gloss: A one-channel condition in which optical power measured after a node is below the expected target.
concepts.example: OCM shows channel 37 at −6 dBm after the ROADM while neighboring channels are −2 dBm.

concepts.label: Passband shifted
concepts.gloss: A one-channel filtering condition in which the WSS transmission passband is displaced from the carrier's center frequency.
concepts.example: The filter center shifts from 193.1 THz to 193.104 THz for one wavelength.

concepts.label: Passband narrowed
concepts.gloss: A one-channel filtering condition in which the WSS transmission bandwidth is smaller than provisioned or required.
concepts.example: A nominal 50 GHz passband contracts enough to clip a 400G signal's spectrum.

concepts.label: signal quality down
concepts.gloss: Reduced recoverability or margin of an optical signal despite possible preservation of its measured power.
concepts.example: A channel retains normal power but its pre-FEC BER rises after WSS filter misalignment.

concepts.label: fails
concepts.gloss: A nonfunctional state of one WSS ingress port.
concepts.example: The west-degree input port ceases switching any wavelength.

concepts.label: blocked
concepts.gloss: A node-local state in which all channels arriving on the degree connected to a failed WSS ingress are prevented from passing.
concepts.example: Every wavelength entering the failed north-degree port is absent at the node's egresses.

concepts.label: unaffected
concepts.gloss: Continued normal operation of ROADM degrees other than the degree served by the failed WSS ingress.
concepts.example: The west degree is blocked, but channels arriving from the east and south degrees continue normally.

concepts.label: Received optical power
concepts.gloss: A monitored measurement of optical power at a receiver, exposed as OPR or its 15-minute statistic and available through standard or power monitoring capability.
concepts.example: OPR-15 reports an average received power of −11.2 dBm for the last interval.

concepts.label: errored seconds
concepts.gloss: A performance counter for seconds containing transmission errors, supplied as the standard ES-15 measurement.
concepts.example: ES-15 records 7 errored seconds in a 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: OSNR
concepts.gloss: A monitored estimate or OCM measurement of optical signal-to-noise ratio requiring advanced monitoring or an OCM licence.
concepts.example: OSNR-EST reports 18.5 dB for a coherent channel.

concepts.label: pre-FEC BER
concepts.gloss: The bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction, available with the advanced monitoring licence.
concepts.example: PREFEC-BER rises from 1×10^-6 to 2×10^-4 as channel margin erodes.

concepts.label: DGD
concepts.gloss: The monitored differential group delay of a coherent optical signal, available through advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: DGD reports 28 ps during a polarization event.

concepts.label: SOP rate of change
concepts.gloss: The measured rate of change of the signal's state of polarization, available through advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: SOP-RATE spikes above the receiver's tracking threshold during fibre movement.

concepts.label: Transmit laser bias current, % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: Transmit-laser bias current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value and reported as LBC under advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: LBC reads 121%, indicating substantial laser ageing.

concepts.label: Composite input power
concepts.gloss: Total optical power across all channels entering an amplifier or optical card, reported as IN-PWR with a power monitoring licence.
concepts.example: IN-PWR on an OLA falls from −6 dBm to −10 dBm after added span loss.

concepts.label: Composite output power
concepts.gloss: Total optical power across all channels leaving an amplifier or optical card, reported as OUT-PWR with a power monitoring licence.
concepts.example: OUT-PWR reads +17 dBm while the amplifier operates at its target.

concepts.label: Pump laser drive current, % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: EDFA pump-laser drive current expressed as a percentage of beginning-of-life current and reported as PUMP-I under advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: PUMP-I reaches 122% and supports diagnosis of pump ageing.

concepts.label: OSC receiver status
concepts.gloss: The standard status indication of whether the optical supervisory-channel receiver is receiving its span OSC.
concepts.example: OSC-RX changes to not received after a span fibre cut.

concepts.label: client ES
concepts.gloss: The client-side errored-seconds counter accumulated in standard 15-minute performance bins.
concepts.example: The current client ES bin contains 12 errored seconds.

concepts.label: client UAS
concepts.gloss: The client-side unavailable-seconds counter accumulated in standard 15-minute performance bins.
concepts.example: A five-minute client outage adds 300 seconds to client UAS.

concepts.label: Per-channel power
concepts.gloss: An OCM-derived optical power measurement for each individual wavelength, available with the OCM licence.
concepts.example: The OCM reports channel 37 at −5.8 dBm while channel 38 is −2.1 dBm.

concepts.label: VA-TPD-400
concepts.gloss: A VA 400G transponder card that terminates a 400G client signal onto an optical channel and can suffer laser, card, receiver, or laser-ageing faults.
concepts.example: A VA-TPD-400 carries one 400G wavelength and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL when its line laser fails.

concepts.label: VA-MXP-200
concepts.gloss: A VA 200G muxponder card that aggregates client traffic onto a 200G optical line signal and is subject to laser, card, receiver, and ageing faults.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-200 transports aggregated clients until receiver degradation causes rising pre-FEC errors.

concepts.label: VA-MXP-400
concepts.gloss: A VA 400G muxponder card that aggregates client traffic onto a 400G optical line signal and is subject to laser, card, receiver, and ageing faults.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-400 loses its transmit laser and the remote end reports OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: VA-OTN-LC-200
concepts.gloss: A VA 200G OTN line card providing an OTN optical line interface and supporting diagnosis of laser, card, receiver, and ageing faults.
concepts.example: A VA-OTN-LC-200 detects a local receiver degradation while other channels remain normal.

concepts.label: VA-OTN-LC-400
concepts.gloss: A VA 400G OTN line card providing an OTN optical line interface and supporting diagnosis of laser, card, receiver, and ageing faults.
concepts.example: A VA-OTN-LC-400 raises LASER_BIAS_HIGH when LBC exceeds 120%.

concepts.label: EDFA card
concepts.gloss: The family of VA booster, in-line, and pre-amplifier EDFA cards that amplify all traversing channels and can experience death, gain, noise, pump, or tilt faults.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA with ageing pumps raises AMP_PUMP_EOL while maintaining span gain.

concepts.label: transmit-side EDFA (booster), fitted at the head end of each optical multiplex section (OMS)
concepts.gloss: A transmit-side EDFA installed at the head of an optical multiplex section to launch the multiplexed channels into the span.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-BST raises the 80-channel composite signal to the provisioned launch power.

concepts.label: optical line amplifier (OLA), fitted at in-line amplifier huts
concepts.gloss: An in-line optical line amplifier installed in an intermediate hut to compensate for preceding or following span attenuation.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA at hut B amplifies channels between two fibre spans and raises AMP_INPUT_LOS if incoming light disappears.

concepts.label: receive-side EDFA (pre-amp), fitted at the tail end of each OMS
concepts.gloss: A receive-side EDFA installed at the tail of an optical multiplex section to amplify channels before node reception.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-PRE at the terminal receives the incoming OMS and raises OMS_LOS_P after its jumper is removed.

concepts.label: OTN cross-connect switch
concepts.gloss: A VA OTN cross-connect that switches ODUs between ports and may suffer fabric failure or logical misconnection.
concepts.example: VA-OTNSW cross-connects ODU2 from a line card to a client port.

concepts.label: client interface port
concepts.gloss: A VA client-facing interface and optic for terminating Ethernet service, susceptible to port failure and used to report client and ODU alarms.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-100GE terminates a 100GE service and raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL when its optic fails.

concepts.label: colourless, directionless, contentionless ROADM
concepts.gloss: A colourless, directionless, contentionless VA ROADM that independently routes wavelengths through WSS elements and can exhibit attenuation, passband, or ingress-port faults.
concepts.example: VA-ROADM-CDC routes the same wavelength from any add port to the east degree.

concepts.label: one WSS module per degree
concepts.gloss: The wavelength-selective-switch module dedicated to one directional degree of a CDC ROADM.
concepts.example: The west degree of a VA-ROADM-CDC uses one WSS module to receive and route all west-arriving channels.

concepts.label: OCH_LOS
concepts.gloss: An optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm raised when a receiver detects no light, with possible causes including transmitter, card, fibre, amplifier, jumper, or WSS-ingress failure.
concepts.example: OCH_LOS is raised at the receiver after an upstream fibre cut removes the wavelength.

concepts.label: OTU_LOF
concepts.gloss: An OTU loss-of-frame alarm raised when light is present but OTU framing is lost because signal quality is severely impaired.
concepts.example: OTU_LOF occurs with normal received power after a shifted WSS passband prevents frame recovery.

concepts.label: OTU_SD
concepts.gloss: An OTU signal-degrade alarm raised when errors exceed the degrade threshold, usually with roughly less than 1 dB of margin remaining.
concepts.example: OTU_SD is raised when contaminated-connector loss drives PREFEC-BER over its threshold.

concepts.label: OTU_BDI
concepts.gloss: An OTU backward-defect-indication alarm showing that the far end has detected a defect in this endpoint's transmitted OTU signal.
concepts.example: The local terminal reports OTU_BDI after the remote receiver loses frame.

concepts.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An equipment alarm identifying a detected transmit-laser fault and therefore a probable transmit-laser failure.
concepts.example: EQPT_TX_FAIL is raised when laser drive is present but no line output is detected.

concepts.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An equipment alarm identifying an internal card hardware fault and probable card failure.
concepts.example: A failed onboard power rail causes a VA-MXP-400 to raise EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

concepts.label: LASER_BIAS_HIGH
concepts.gloss: An incipient laser-ageing alarm raised when transmit-laser bias current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: LASER_BIAS_HIGH appears when LBC reaches 123%.

concepts.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
concepts.gloss: An OLA alarm raised when IN-PWR indicates loss of incoming light, commonly due to a fibre break, excessive span loss, or failure of the preceding EDFA.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA raises AMP_INPUT_LOS after the upstream span is cut.

concepts.label: OMS_LOS_P
concepts.gloss: A pre-amplifier alarm raised when light is lost at the OMS input, potentially due to fibre, span-loss, preceding-amplifier, or jumper faults.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-PRE raises OMS_LOS_P when its OMS input jumper is pulled.

concepts.label: OSC_LOS
concepts.gloss: An alarm indicating that the span optical supervisory channel is not received, typically because of a fibre break or excessive span loss.
concepts.example: OSC_LOS is raised at hut C when the B–C supervisory wavelength disappears.

concepts.label: AMP_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An EDFA-card failure alarm raised when input light is present but the amplifier produces no output light.
concepts.example: AMP_FAIL is raised on a VA-OA-BST whose pumps have stopped despite valid IN-PWR.

concepts.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
concepts.gloss: An amplifier gain-out-of-range alarm raised when measured gain differs from target by more than 2 dB, implicating dead, weakened, or ageing amplifier components.
concepts.example: AMP_GAIN_OOR is raised when actual gain is 16 dB against a 19 dB target.

concepts.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
concepts.gloss: An EDFA end-of-life alarm raised when pump current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value due to pump ageing.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-PRE raises AMP_PUMP_EOL at PUMP-I 121%.

concepts.label: CLIENT_SF
concepts.gloss: A client-port signal-fail alarm indicating unavailable client traffic, with possible causes in the port, ODU routing, switch fabric, or wider service path.
concepts.example: CLIENT_SF is raised on a 100GE port after a fabric failure stops its ODU.

concepts.label: ODU_AIS
concepts.gloss: A client-port alarm indicating receipt of ODU alarm-indication signal from an upstream defect.
concepts.example: ODU_AIS appears at the client port after OTU frame loss causes downstream AIS insertion.

concepts.label: ODU_BDI
concepts.gloss: A client-port alarm indicating receipt of ODU backward defect indication from the downstream end of the ODU trail.
concepts.example: ODU_BDI is reported when the remote ODU termination detects a trail defect.

concepts.label: ODU_TIM
concepts.gloss: A client-port ODU trail-trace-identifier mismatch alarm that commonly reveals a misdirected or misconnected ODU.
concepts.example: ODU_TIM is raised when the received trail identifier belongs to another customer circuit.

concepts.label: PROT_ACTIVE
concepts.gloss: A protection-state alarm indicating that service is currently selected from the protection path because of a failure affecting the working path.
concepts.example: PROT_ACTIVE appears after SNCP switches from a failed working ODU to its clean protection ODU.

concepts.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
concepts.gloss: A protection-state alarm indicating that no defect-free protection path is available to preserve the service.
concepts.example: PROT_UNAVAIL is raised when both working and protection ODUs carry defects.

concepts.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A client-port equipment alarm identifying failure of the port or its optic.
concepts.example: A dead VA-CP-400GE transceiver causes EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

concepts.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An OTN-switch alarm identifying failure of the cross-connect fabric and the resulting risk to all traversing ODUs.
concepts.example: VA-OTNSW raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL when its fabric stops forwarding cross-connected ODUs.

concepts.label: the channel
concepts.gloss: The single optical wavelength channel directly affected by a stated condition.
concepts.example: A failed line laser removes only its associated 400G channel.

concepts.label: the transmitted channel
concepts.gloss: The particular optical channel emitted by the transmitter under discussion.
concepts.example: Laser failure affects the transmitted channel toward the far-end receiver.

concepts.label: received traffic
concepts.gloss: Traffic arriving at and being delivered by the local receiving function.
concepts.example: A local card failure removes all received traffic from its client outputs.

concepts.label: monitoring
concepts.gloss: The telemetry, status, and performance-reporting functions of the relevant equipment.
concepts.example: After a control-processor failure, monitoring for the card becomes silent.

concepts.label: traffic alarms
concepts.gloss: Lower-level alarms associated with carried traffic rather than the equipment itself.
concepts.example: OTU and ODU alarms are masked while a dominant card-failure alarm is active.

concepts.label: this receiver only
concepts.gloss: The individual receiver being examined, excluding the shared path and other receivers.
concepts.example: Errors on one coherent receiver do not appear on a second receiver of the same signal.

concepts.label: other channels
concepts.gloss: Optical wavelength channels other than the specifically impaired channel.
concepts.example: Other channels remain normal when one receiver degrades.

concepts.label: the optical path
concepts.gloss: The end-to-end optical route and common transmission elements carrying the channel.
concepts.example: The optical path remains healthy when errors originate solely in the terminal receiver.

concepts.label: LBC
concepts.gloss: The transmit laser-bias-current measurement used to track laser ageing.
concepts.example: LBC rises from 100% to 120% over the laser's lifetime.

concepts.label: transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: The future complete failure of the transmit laser to which an incipient condition relates.
concepts.example: High LBC is treated as a precursor to transmit laser failure.

concepts.label: the channel's margin
concepts.gloss: The affected channel's remaining tolerance to additional optical impairment before errors or failure occur.
concepts.example: A channel margin decreases from 3 dB to 0.8 dB.

concepts.label: all channels
concepts.gloss: Every optical wavelength sharing the affected common element or line section.
concepts.example: A dead EDFA removes all channels that traverse it.

concepts.label: every channel downstream
concepts.gloss: Every wavelength channel propagated beyond the affected point in the downstream direction.
concepts.example: An amplifier noise penalty appears on every channel downstream of that amplifier.

concepts.label: this card
concepts.gloss: The particular equipment card on which the condition is measured or alarmed.
concepts.example: Rising PUMP-I and AMP_PUMP_EOL are local to one VA-OA-PRE card.

concepts.label: channels at one band edge
concepts.gloss: The subset of wavelength channels located near one edge of the amplifier's supported optical band.
concepts.example: Gain tilt leaves only the highest-frequency edge channels low.

concepts.label: All ODUs
concepts.gloss: Every Optical Data Unit cross-connected through the affected OTN switch or fabric.
concepts.example: A fabric failure interrupts all ODUs traversing the switch.

concepts.label: each
concepts.gloss: Each individual member of the contextually identified affected set.
concepts.example: The switch forwards AIS on each impacted ODU.

concepts.label: One ODU
concepts.gloss: A single Optical Data Unit trail, rather than all ODUs on the optical carrier or switch.
concepts.example: A misconnection sends one ODU to the wrong destination.

concepts.label: Client optic
concepts.gloss: The pluggable or integrated optical transceiver serving a client interface.
concepts.example: A failed 100GE client optic causes its port to fail.

concepts.label: port
concepts.gloss: The individual physical or logical interface on the equipment card.
concepts.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL applies to client port 3 only.

concepts.label: client service
concepts.gloss: The customer-facing service carried through the associated client port and ODU path.
concepts.example: The 100GE client service goes down when its port optic fails.

concepts.label: one channel
concepts.gloss: Exactly one wavelength channel selected or impaired independently of neighboring channels.
concepts.example: WSS attenuation drift makes channel 37 low while channel 38 remains normal.

concepts.label: One WSS input port
concepts.gloss: A single ingress port of a wavelength-selective switch serving one ROADM degree.
concepts.example: Failure is confined to the WSS port connected to the west degree.

concepts.label: all channels arriving on that degree
concepts.gloss: All wavelength channels arriving at a ROADM on the same directional degree.
concepts.example: A failed north-degree ingress blocks every channel arriving from the north.

concepts.label: other degrees
concepts.gloss: ROADM directional interfaces other than the degree containing the identified fault.
concepts.example: East and south degrees remain operational when the west ingress fails.

concepts.label: the far-end receiver
concepts.gloss: The remote optical receiver at the destination of the locally transmitted channel.
concepts.example: A local laser failure is observed as loss of signal at the far-end receiver.

concepts.label: Far-end
concepts.gloss: The remote endpoint opposite the locally observed network or service endpoint.
concepts.example: The far end returns BDI after detecting a defect.

concepts.label: locally
concepts.gloss: At the network element or endpoint currently being examined, rather than at its remote peer.
concepts.example: A card failure causes received traffic to be lost locally.

concepts.label: the receiver
concepts.gloss: The optical receiving function where incoming power, quality, and margin are observed.
concepts.example: Slow margin decline is measured at the coherent receiver.

concepts.label: Far-end transmitter
concepts.gloss: The remote transmitting function toward which a backward defect indication is returned.
concepts.example: OTU-BDI is sent back to the far-end transmitter after local frame loss.

concepts.label: Anywhere upstream on the channel's path
concepts.gloss: Any point earlier along the channel's propagation path that could cause a downstream observation.
concepts.example: OCH_LOS at a receiver may originate from a fibre cut anywhere upstream.

concepts.label: Upstream on the path
concepts.gloss: The portion of the service or optical route before the observation point in the direction of signal flow.
concepts.example: A dirty connector on the upstream path degrades the received channel.

concepts.label: This card
concepts.gloss: The physical card currently reporting or exhibiting the condition.
concepts.example: PUMP-I is measured on this amplifier card, not on the preceding EDFA.

concepts.label: on the path to the far end
concepts.gloss: A point along the route leading from the local endpoint toward the remote endpoint.
concepts.example: A fibre fault on the path to the far end causes remote loss of signal.

concepts.label: downstream
concepts.gloss: At network elements or endpoints reached after the fault in the direction of traffic propagation.
concepts.example: ODU-AIS is sent downstream from the OTU receiver.

concepts.label: one band edge
concepts.gloss: The low- or high-frequency boundary region of the optical amplification band.
concepts.example: Channels at the high-frequency band edge are low because of gain tilt.

concepts.label: on the incoming span
concepts.gloss: The fibre span delivering optical signals into the current amplifier, terminal, or node.
concepts.example: A break on the incoming span causes the OLA's IN-PWR to disappear.

concepts.label: previous EDFA
concepts.gloss: The nearest upstream EDFA whose output feeds the current span or receiver.
concepts.example: If the previous EDFA dies, the next OLA raises AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: OMS input
concepts.gloss: The physical input point of an optical multiplex section at its receiving amplifier or node.
concepts.example: Pulling the jumper at the OMS input causes OMS_LOS_P.

concepts.label: through the switch
concepts.gloss: Across the internal OTN cross-connect path from a switch ingress to its configured egress.
concepts.example: All ODUs passing through the switch are interrupted by fabric failure.

concepts.label: on the active ODU path
concepts.gloss: The ODU branch currently selected to carry the protected client service.
concepts.example: After protection switching, the protection branch becomes the active ODU path.

concepts.label: at either end
concepts.gloss: At either termination endpoint of a bidirectional service or ODU trail.
concepts.example: A port failure at either end can make the client service unavailable.

concepts.label: at a switch on the ODU path
concepts.gloss: An OTN switch situated on the end-to-end ODU route.
concepts.example: A misconnection at a switch on the ODU path sends the payload to the wrong client.

concepts.label: on the working ODU path
concepts.gloss: The primary ODU route used under normal SNCP operation.
concepts.example: A fibre fault on the working ODU path causes selection of protection.

concepts.label: on the protection ODU path
concepts.gloss: The alternate ODU route reserved or concurrently carried for SNCP protection.
concepts.example: The selector chooses the protection ODU path when the working copy has AIS.

concepts.label: This port
concepts.gloss: The specific local interface currently reporting or experiencing the condition.
concepts.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL identifies a fault on this client port.

concepts.label: This switch
concepts.gloss: The particular local OTN cross-connect being examined.
concepts.example: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL indicates that the defect is in this switch.

concepts.label: after the node
concepts.gloss: On the outgoing side of the current network node after its switching and power-leveling functions.
concepts.example: One wavelength measures low after the ROADM because its WSS attenuation drifted.

concepts.label: at the node
concepts.gloss: Within or at the boundaries of the current ROADM or switching site.
concepts.example: Channels on a failed ingress degree are blocked at the node.

concepts.label: Standard
concepts.gloss: Monitoring functionality included by default without an optional feature licence.
concepts.example: ES-15 and OSC-RX are readable with the standard package.

concepts.label: Power monitoring licence
concepts.gloss: An optional entitlement enabling optical power measurements such as OPR, IN-PWR, and OUT-PWR.
concepts.example: After enabling the power monitoring licence, an operator can graph amplifier IN-PWR.

concepts.label: Advanced monitoring licence
concepts.gloss: An optional entitlement enabling advanced coherent and equipment metrics such as OSNR estimate, pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP rate, LBC, and PUMP-I.
concepts.example: The advanced licence exposes PREFEC-BER and SOP-RATE on a VA-TPD-400.

concepts.label: 15-minute bins (standard)
concepts.gloss: Standard availability of client performance counters as accumulated 15-minute measurement intervals.
concepts.example: Client ES and UAS are retrieved for the previous 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: OCM licence
concepts.gloss: An optional entitlement enabling optical-channel-monitor measurements such as per-channel power and measured OSNR.
concepts.example: With the OCM licence, the operator compares power and OSNR for all wavelengths.

concepts.label: Hard
concepts.gloss: A fault nature representing an abrupt, definitive failure that normally causes immediate loss of traffic or signal.
concepts.example: A fibre cut producing complete OCH_LOS is classified as hard.

concepts.label: Soft
concepts.gloss: A fault nature representing a degradative impairment that reduces quality or margin while service may continue.
concepts.example: Noise-figure degradation causing OTU_SD but not loss of traffic is classified as soft.

concepts.label: Incipient
concepts.gloss: A fault nature representing an early warning trend that precedes likely component failure.
concepts.example: Rising LBC from laser ageing is classified as incipient.

concepts.label: Critical
concepts.gloss: The highest alarm impact class, used for conditions requiring immediate action because service or major capacity is lost.
concepts.example: A fabric failure interrupting all ODUs is assigned Critical severity.

concepts.label: Minor
concepts.gloss: A low alarm impact class for conditions needing attention but not presently causing major service loss.
concepts.example: An early laser-bias warning with traffic intact is assigned Minor severity.

concepts.label: Not alarmed
concepts.gloss: A classification for a monitored state or symptom that does not itself generate an alarm.
concepts.example: A gradual margin decline may be visible in telemetry but classified as Not alarmed.

concepts.label: Major
concepts.gloss: A high alarm impact class below critical, typically indicating significant degradation or loss of a service or equipment function.
concepts.example: Failure of one client port and its service is assigned Major severity.

concepts.label: On loss of OTU frame, G.798 consequent actions apply: ODU-AIS is sent downstream on every ODU in the OTU, and OTU-BDI is returned to the far-end transmitter.
concepts.gloss: The G.798 response to OTU frame loss whereby every contained ODU is replaced with downstream ODU-AIS and OTU-BDI is returned upstream to the far-end transmitter.
concepts.example: When an OTU receiver loses frame, it inserts AIS on all tributary ODUs and sends BDI back to the transmitter.

concepts.label: Every hut terminates the optical supervisory channel (OSC) and launches its own OSC onto the next span.
concepts.gloss: The supervisory-channel regeneration model in which each amplifier hut terminates the incoming OSC and originates a separate OSC on the next span.
concepts.example: An OSC failure on span A–B ends at hut B because hut B independently launches the OSC for B–C.

concepts.label: Client services may be protected with SNCP: a working and a protection ODU path, with the selector at the receiving client port.
concepts.gloss: A client-service protection arrangement using working and protection ODU copies with receive-side selection at the client port.
concepts.example: When the working ODU develops AIS, the receiving client port selects the defect-free protection ODU with only a brief hit.

concepts.label: Switching is per channel at each egress degree. A line-wide impairment on an ingress degree therefore continues as a per-channel impairment on each channel routed onward.
concepts.gloss: The ROADM forwarding model in which wavelengths are switched independently at each egress, so a degree-wide ingress impairment persists separately on every onward-routed channel.
concepts.example: An OSNR penalty affecting all west-ingress wavelengths remains on each channel after some are routed east and others south.
